comment: Ground truth for the user's own library (established by ear + analysis). Values are DETECTOR-relative: rot = allowed values of (downbeat index % beatsPerBar) on the detector's own beat grid; bpb = expected beatsPerBar. null = no stable ground truth, report only. reject:true = the detector must return null (no steady pulse deserves a metronome). barLenAt = [{t, n}]: the bar covering time t must be n beats long — the only anchor that catches an un-modelled meter change (a uniform-4 grid reports 4 everywhere and silently stretches the odd bar). Sourced from the published score AND verified against the audio before being committed.

Dreamer.scoreNote: TWO official transcriptions agree (guitar Pro x2): quarter = 78 (ours 79.5 ✓), UNIFORM 4/4, 93 bars, no meter changes anywhere. The outro drops to quarter = 61 at bar 93 — but that is the final let-ring chord, not a played tempo. Our single stretched bar (269.56, claims 4 lasts 3.58) sits exactly at the outro transition where the band stops: a ring-out boundary, not meter. Dreamer is the THIRD negative control after TTP and Crowley — a bar decoder must leave it alone.

Going To The Run.scoreNote: THREE FINDINGS, one of them serious. Official Golden Earring tab: quarter = 124, uniform 4/4 across all 121 bars, no repeats. (1) WE SHIP 62.3 bpm — EXACTLY HALF the notated tempo, and this is a GT ANCHOR song (rot 2/4, barAt 144.033). Same direction and magnitude as Puppe, whose ear verdict (2026-08-02) chose the FASTER notated reading; that precedent puts the thumb on 124 here too, but it needs its own ear check before anything is changed — the anchors depend on it. Corroborating evidence that our grid is confused: our downbeats[] is a MIX of 22 two-beat bars and 50 four-beat bars, which is exactly what a half-tempo lattice looks like when some bars are counted at the notated level (2 of our beats) and others at twice that. (2) A notated tempo change we click through: quarter = 83 for the FINAL TWO BARS (bar 120, on the last sung word "An-gel", ~3:50 onward, with cresc. hairpins) — our tail holds 62-63 bpm flat. That is the FIFTH notated ending tempo event in this library (WDOA, SoF, Puppe, Dreamer, GTTR). (3) STRUCTURAL, matters for phase 5b/5c: the section lengths are 9/8/9/8/9/16/8/8/9/16/21 bars — every PRE-CHORUS IS NINE BARS and so is the intro, with no meter change anywhere. Anything that assumes 8-bar phrases mis-phases from 0:32.9 on. Vocal phrases also start with a pickup in the bar BEFORE each section label. Score prints no chord symbols; harmonic rhythm read off bass/rhythm voicings is one chord per bar, sometimes tied across two.

Mr Crowley.note: slip-class song; two harmonic phase slips (126.6s, 166.5s) re-phased since v9 — anchor minted from the harmonically-validated grid (chord changes 86% on bar starts)
Mr Crowley.scoreNote: Two official transcriptions agree (vocal + bass): Intro quarter = 90, then 105 at Verse 1 (bar 20), uniform 4/4 throughout, 126 bars, no meter changes. Both our tempos confirmed: measured 90.9 intro / 107.7 body vs notated 90/105 — the v12 organ-intro splice ("own tempo under the body") is exactly what the page says. Therefore the 24 stretched bars the sweep flagged (most in the library) are PERFORMANCE looseness — pushed fills, organ rubato — already the defect-splice family's job, and NOT meter. Do not let a future bar decoder mint odd bars here; this song joins TTP as a negative control, at 5x the difficulty.

Nothing Else Matters.scoreNote: Ultimate-Guitar official score: 6/8 with 3/8 bars at bar 7 (intro), 57/73/117 (end of each chorus, on "Oh, but I know") and 142/147 (outro); dotted-quarter = 72. Our grid is 154 bars, ALL 6 beats. NOT anchored: at the chorus ends the score points to, our bars measure a clean 5.92-6.17 beats — no short bar — so either we absorb the 3/8 invisibly (which would shift bar phase by half a bar afterwards) or the score bar numbers do not map where assumed. The three stretched bars we DO have (198.93, 201.25, 317.07) sit in instrumental/outro regions, and the outro is where the score puts its last two 3/8 bars. Revisit when the bar decoder lands — this is the one score-vs-audio disagreement in the set and it needs an ear, not more arithmetic.

Panzerkampf.scoreNote: Official Sabaton tab: quarter = 99 (ours 97.5, 1.5% off), UNIFORM 4/4 across all 124 bars, no repeats/DS/coda, harmonic rhythm one chord per bar at fastest (whole Intro/Verse 1/every Chorus sit on a single F#5). FOURTH negative control after TTP, Crowley and Dreamer — a bar decoder must leave it alone. Independently cross-checked two ways: 124 bars at 99 = 300.6 s vs the player's 5:01, and the PARTS timeline's per-section pixel widths match the printed bar counts to within 1 px (any odd bar would have shifted a section visibly). NOTE we emit no downbeats[] here — scalar rotation only. READING TRAP: the vocal line carries QUINTUPLET brackets (a bracketed "5" at bars 15, 23, 48, 56, 58) and triplets at 77 — those are tuplets on the vocal rhythm, NOT 5/4 or 3/4 bars, and a pixel-reading pass will mistake them for meter marks.

Puppe.scoreNote: Official Rammstein tab: quarter = 117 — the notation sides with the eval harness's 117.8, AGAINST the 58.73 we ship (measured exactly half, 1.99x). The v15 doc stance stands — half-vs-double is taste and the singer's pending ear verdict decides — but the notation thumb is now on the fast side, and v16's mlBimodal measured Puppe 0.26-0.27 (the model itself wavers). Meter: uniform 4/4 for 128 bars, then an outro tempo staircase 117 -> 100 (bar 128) -> 75 (bar 130) with a single 3/4 at bar 129. Our outro spacing (1.0 s +/- 0.15 noisy) shows no clear staircase — but that region is the known trailing-void knife edge, and trailing voids never splice, so low stakes today. The one interior grid hole at 37.88 has NO notated counterpart (uniform 4/4 there) — a real defect, not music.

Sixteen Tons.note: harmonic re-phase v9: plain grid explained 4.6% of chord changes, re-phased 59% — anchor from the harmonically-validated grid; EAR-CHECK PENDING

Soldier Of Fortune.scoreNote: Official Deep Purple tab (quarter = 66; ours 67.1 ✓): 4/4 with a 2/4 bar at every "windmill going round" — score bars 18, 43, 48. Audio-consistent at all three: windmill->round spans 1.8-1.9 beats at 61.7/149.7/165.8, i.e. the 2/4 carries "windmill going" and "round" opens the next 4/4. One anchor minted at the cleanest instance (verse-2 chorus, t=150.5 want 2 — RED today, we claim 4); the other two are recorded, not minted. Our grid swallows the first two 2/4s with no anomaly at all and shows one 4.47-beat stretched bar at 180.33. ALSO: notated rall. at bar 52, 66 -> 38, on the final "soldier of fortune" — our outro spacing stays 0.89-0.92 s flat, so the click races the band if the recording really slows (same ending class as WDOA; needs an ear). This is a GT ANCHOR song: rot/barAt still pass because the ear-minted barAt is real, but the uniform grid must be re-syncing across the swallowed 2/4s via slips — the phase between choruses is not to be trusted.

The Music Of The Night.scoreNote: REFUSAL VINDICATED BY NOTATION (licensed vocal score, 2026-08-03). The published score's FIRST marking is "Slowly, with freedom (quarter = 64)" — the composer instructs rubato in bar 1 — and the piece then carries: accel. at bar 13-14, "Faster (quarter = 76)" at bar 15, two FERMATAS at bar 20, "Very slowly" at bar 21, "a tempo" at 22-23, and a closing rit. + fermata at bar 44. So there is no single tempo to find: our detector rejects this song with "windows disagree on a tempo (rubato?)" and the windows disagree because the music genuinely does. This is the only song in the library whose detector behaviour is confirmed correct BY THE COMPOSER'S OWN INSTRUCTION rather than by ear. Keep reject:true; never "fix" it by inventing a grid. Bonus: the score is also NOT uniform 4/4 — 2/4 bars at 10, 29-30 and 40-41 — so a forced grid would have been wrong in three independent ways at once (tempo, tempo CHANGES, and meter). Earlier note stands as method: Ultimate Guitar could not settle this (whole Phantom catalogue rights-blocked); an engraved vocal score could, because only engraved scores carry rall./a tempo/fermata at all.

Turn The Page.note: barAtMl = the bass-solo bars (201-227s spliced span), ear-approved 2026-08-01: the v14 span-phase vote lands them on the bass chord changes (margin 0.73; blind extension missed by ~1.5 beats; the model alone only half-bar-marks here). The 225s +2-beat re-entry odd bar remains the v5 fermata case.
Turn The Page.scoreNote: Official Metallica bass tab (D# G# C# F#, "Moderately Slow" quarter = 76; ours reads 74.9 — right octave): 112 bars, 4/4 at bar 1 and NEVER AGAIN. This is the counter-example the bar decoder needs — a song with five stretched bars that are NOT meter changes and must stay 4 beats. The barLenAt entries above pin exactly those five spots and pass today; they exist to fail if a decoder starts inventing odd bars wherever the tracker wobbles. OPEN QUESTION: we emit one 2-beat bar at 224.99 which the score does not have. That is the "+2 beats at the last chorus" the v5 fermata mechanics were built around, measured from the audio — a transcription normalises what a live-feel performance breathes, so score and recording may both be right. Needs an ear before it becomes an anchor either way.

Wanted Dead Or Alive.note: beatAtMl = the 48-93s drum-void the v8 gate refuses: v10 coasted through it and drifted up to half a beat (user heard it); v11 splices the model lattice there — ear-approved 2026-07-31. Anchors are BEAT times from the approved grid (coasting misses them by 330/335/104ms). v9's 204.8s breakdown re-phase rode along in that listen.
Wanted Dead Or Alive.scoreNote: Official Bon Jovi bass tab (E A D G, quarter = 74 — our 74.90 is the closest tempo match in the set): 4/4 with ONE 2/4 bar at score bar 62, at the chorus exit "dead or a-li-ve" before Verse 3. Same shape as Wild World: a half-bar where a chorus hands over. We emit exactly one odd bar in the song too — a SIX-beat bar at 202.23 — and 4+2 = 6, so we may be MERGING the odd bar where the score SPLITS it. That distinction is audible: 4+2 accents the start of the 2, a single 6 does not. Not positionally verified (lyric anchoring has been unreliable against these transcriptions), so no anchor. A bar decoder should prefer 4+2 over 6 when the evidence supports a bar line in the middle — this is the test case for that. SECOND finding, different class: the score notates a ritardando on the sustained ending (quarter = 66 at bar 90, then 48 at bar 91). Our grid holds ~0.79 s to the last beat at 307.6 s and never slows. Either the recording holds rather than slows, or we coast a click through a rallentando — the doc already flags "WDOA outro fade" as a real-music defect zone. Needs an ear.

Zeit.scoreNote: TWO official transcriptions agree (bass tab + piano/vocal, both quarter = 61, both placing every mark identically): 4/4 with a 2/4 at bar 26 ("weitergeh'n" -> Interlude) and bar 39 ("Schon ist der Moment vorbei" -> Chorus) — chorus/section exits again, like every other odd bar in the catalog. We ship 123.0 bpm, exactly DOUBLE the notation (the Puppe situation again — Rammstein ballads notated slow, shipped double; mlBimodal measured 0.12 here). THE STRUCTURAL INSIGHT THIS SONG ADDS: at our doubled level a notated 2/4 spans exactly ONE of our 4-beat bars, so the phase shift is SELF-ABSORBING — our grid crosses both 2/4s without any parity error, which is why the sweep saw no swallowed-bar signature here. The octave decision changes which meter changes are dangerous: at notated tempo (Wild World, FaS) a 2/4 breaks the grid; at double (Zeit, Puppe) it vanishes. A future bar decoder must reason about meter AT THE NOTATED LEVEL. The 8 stretched bars + 13 holes the sweep flagged live in the piano-only intro/outro (9 bars each, near-silent bass/drums — fill-tracking territory), not at the 2/4s. No anchors minted: nothing here is red at our level.

Cat Stevens — Father and Son.note: TWO independent official transcriptions agree (vocal score + rhythm-guitar Pro tab, both quarter=67): 4/4 with 5/4 at score bar 19 and 3/4 at bars 30, 41, 60. Both odd-bar anchors are audio-verified, not just page-read. The 5/4: bar 19 spans "still"@66.20 -> "not"@70.55 = 4.94 beats. The 3/4 at the first Break: our own grid agrees with the score up to its bar line at 104.36, the tab puts "I know I have to" inside that bar (sung 105.64-106.75, contained), and "go" — which opens the next 4/4 — lands at 106.99 = 2.99 beats after 104.36. Our grid claims 4 (next bar at 108.00). The v3 break (score bar 60) is NOT anchored: by then two upstream meter changes have shifted our uniform grid's phase ("go" v3 sits a beat past our 209.44 bar line), so a time anchor there would encode our own error. The guitar tab also documents the strum as a per-half-bar cell (down-up + muted X, twice per bar) — the notated confirmation of the measured lag-2 strum ACF: the accompaniment is half-bar periodic BY ARRANGEMENT, and the v17 grid emits 58 bars all 4 beats with a bar line inside the 5/4.

Wild World.note: MSB full score: quarter = 74 (our 76.9 confirms the OCTAVE — the pre-v16 156.6 was wrong), 4/4 with 2/4 bars at 12, 29 and 46, one at the end of each verse. Two chords per bar (Am D / G C / F Dm), which is why the chord-change cue is structurally half-bar periodic here and cannot name the "1". v17 emits 59 bars, all 4 beats. A 2/4 bar shifts the phase by exactly 2 beats — the "which half-bar is the 1" ambiguity is a real meter change, not a tie. No time-anchored bar yet: the score is a different lyric transcription from ours, so word-level anchoring was unreliable (measured 7.07 beats where the score implies 6). Needs an ear verdict before anchors are minted.
